output.summary: A creeping succulent native to coastal North Africa and Sinai, the Levant, maritime southern Europe, and several Mediterranean and North Atlantic islands. Glistening water-filled cells cover the plant, and its many-petalled flowers open by morning and close at night. The leaves and seeds are edible; the plant has been promoted and commercially grown as a vegetable.
output.edibilityNote: Leaves and seeds are edible; it was formerly promoted as a spinach-like vegetable and is now sold commercially in Japan.
